questions.stem: A patient who is a known case of HIV is started on combined active antiretroviral therapy (cART). After 5 months of treatment, he develops hyperpigmentation in the nails. What is the most likely drug causing this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Zidovudine
  • Zidovudine is a synthetic analog of the nucleoside thymidine classified as a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI). Zidovudine functions as an antiviral agent by being incorporated into newly made viral DNA in place of thymidine and acting as a viral DNA chain terminator.


Basic & Clinical Pharmacology Katzung, 14th Edition, Page No. 912

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pharmacology - INI CET NOVEMBER 2022 (PART - A)
questions.stem: What is the appropriate serum plasma concentration of lithium for treatment and prophylaxis of mania?
questions.solutionHtml:
0.6-1.5 mEq/L
  • Mania is a period of 1 week or more in which a person experiences a change in normal behaviour that drastically affects their functioning.
  • The defining characteristics of mania include increased talkativeness, rapid speech, a decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, distractibility, increase in goal-directed activity, and psychomotor agitation.
  • The therapeutic range is 1.0 to 1.5 mEq/L for acute treatment and 0.6 to 1.2 mEq/L for chronic therapy.
  • Monitoring should be done every 1 to 2 weeks until reaching the desired therapeutic levels. Then, check lithium levels every 2 to 3 months for six months.
  • It is also important to monitor patients for dehydration and lower the dose when there are signs of infection, excessive sweating, or diarrhea.
  • Toxic levels are when the drug level is more than 2 mEq/L.


Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th Edition, Page No. 397

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pharmacology - INI CET NOVEMBER 2022 (PART - A)
questions.stem: Hemolysis in glucose 6 phosphate deficiency can manifest with which of the following drugs:
questions.solutionHtml:
Primaquine
  • G6PD deficiency is an X-linked recessive disorder that causes congenital hemolytic anaemia due to enzyme deficiency.
  • Hemolysis occurs in conditions of high oxidative stress that are triggered by infections, fava beans, and certain drugs.
  • G6PD is an enzyme in the hexose monophosphate pathway (HMP) that maintains the cellular levels of NADPH. NADPH then provides reducing equivalents needed for the conversion of oxidised glutathione to reduced glutathione. Reduced glutathione helps neutralise free radicals, protecting against oxidant injury.
  • Clinically, most patients are asymptomatic.
  • Both primaquine and chloroquine cause hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals, but hemolysis is rare with chloroquine and it can be used in patients with G6PD deficiency, whereas primaquine is contraindicated in these individuals.


Basic & Clinical Pharmacology Katzung, 14th Edition, Page No. 983
